newsitem.title: USA: GM Oldsmobile general manager to retire.
newsitem.headline: GM Oldsmobile general manager to retire.

text.p: John Rock, general manager of General Motors Corp's Oldsmobile division, will retire and be replaced by Darwin Clark, currently vice president of sales, marketing and after-sales for GM in Euorpe, a company spokesman said Monday.
Rock plans to leave January 1, 1997. Clark will join the organization November 1 so the two can work jointly on the transition, said Oldsmobile spokesman Peter Ternes.
Rock, 60 years old, has been at Oldsmobile for four and one-half years. An article in Monday's Detroit Free Press said Rock clashed with Ronald Zarrella, GM's marketing chief.

Zarrella, who has a consumer products background, has been pushing GM to more strongly differentiate individual vehicle brands. Rock is the second division manager to leave GM since Zarrella joined the company about two years ago. Chevrolet General Manager Jim Perkins retired earlier this year.

Rock was not pushed out of his job, said Ternes. In a letter to Oldsmobile employees, Rock said he had been considering retiring for some time but wanted to wait until the division had a stronger product focus and vision.
"John thinks Oldsmobile is set in the right direction," said Ternes. "His decision to retire was just that -- it wasn't being forced."

In a statement, Zarrella said, "John will be missed at General Motors and his dedicated leadership has played a key role in supporting GM's North American Operations turn around over the past several years."

Oldsmobile, the oldest surviving nameplate in the U.S. auto industry, has been suffering a sales decline since hitting its peak in 1985 with 1.07 million units, as it struggles to attract younger buyers and compete with imports.

Speaking to reporters in September, Rock said he expects the division's sales to fall to 330,000 vehicles in 1997 -- its lowest since 1961 -- from about 340,000 to 350,000 in 1996. Sales this year through September were 256,141, down 14.3 percent.

Rock, whose colorful, plain-talking demeanor made him a favorite among dealers, began at GM's Buick division in 1960 and rose through several sales positions. Clark started with the automaker in 1959 on the engineering staff at Buick. Clark has been in his current post since 1992.
